ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Howard Hughes

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for a cough

text.paragraph: Mr. Hughes came in without an appointment with a cough for five days, at first dry and now bringing up a little clear sputum, after a cold that began a week ago. He has had a temperature up to 37.6 °C at home, a sore chest wall when he coughs, and no shortness of breath, wheeze, blood in the sputum or shaking chills. He has been anxious that the cough means a serious infection in the lung injured in the crash, and he has asked his assistant several times a day to check his temperature. He has taken buprenorphine with naloxone 8 mg twice daily for six weeks and sertraline 100 mg for two weeks, without side effects. He wanted to know whether he could take a codeine cough syrup he was given last year. [S]

Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry

text.paragraph: No results recorded at this visit.
Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-22; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired but well; temperature 37.4 °C, pulse 84, respiratory rate 18, blood pressure 120/76, oxygen saturation 97% on room air
Throat mildly red without exudate; ear drums normal
Breathing unlabored; scattered coarse sounds that clear with coughing; no crackles, dullness or wheeze; healed scars of the chest wall

Intrusive fears of contamination by germs for about a year, worse since the crash, with hand washing, cleaning of objects and avoidance of handshakes, shared spaces and food handled by others, taking about four hours a day; he recognizes the fears are probably excessive; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented fear of germs; resolved into the diagnosis of OCD at the consultation. Not a claim about his real symptoms in 1947.
Obsessive-compulsive disorder, contamination type, with good or fair insight, not tic-related; Y-BOCS 28 (severe) at intake; no post-traumatic stress disorder on screening
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, linked to the retrospective interpretation of his documented fears (R). Not a claim about his real diagnosis.

Opioid use disorder, moderate (four of the DSM-5-TR criteria that count for a prescribed opioid: taking more than prescribed, failed attempts to cut down, time spent getting prescriptions from two prescribers, and craving), on codeine prescribed after a crash; buprenorphine planned
S — Synthetic modern coding; tolerance and withdrawal are not counted for a medicine taken under medical supervision. Person-first language; not a claim about his real diagnosis.
Chronic pain after major trauma ten months ago (crushed chest with rib fractures, collapsed lung, other fractures and burns): chest wall, left shoulder and low back pain, PEG 6.7
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented injuries.
Difficulty hearing conversation, worse in noise, after years of flying in loud aircraft; cause under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem; resolved into a diagnosis when audiometry was done at five weeks. His documented deafness is from later years.
Bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss with a notch at 4000 Hz, consistent with noise exposure from flying; hearing aids fitted
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at five weeks; not a claim about his real hearing in 1947.
Weight loss of about 8 kg since the crash (BMI 19.7), from eating little outside food he has prepared or inspected himself because of contamination fears
S — Synthetic nutrition problem linked to the contamination fears; not a claim about his real weight in 1947.
Acute bronchitis, likely viral, for five days; no pneumonia on examination; resolved within three weeks without antibiotics
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Acute bronchitis, likely viral (J20.9). His pulse is under 100, his respiratory rate under 24, his temperature under 38 °C and his chest examination shows no sign of consolidation, so pneumonia is unlikely and a chest X-ray and antibiotics are not needed, in line with ACP and CDC advice. His old lung injury does not change this, and his oxygen saturation is normal. The cough may last up to three weeks. [S]
Honey, warm fluids and rest.
His scheduled acetaminophen continues; no extra doses.
Return or call for shortness of breath, a temperature above 38.5 °C, blood in the sputum, or a cough that is worsening after three weeks.

Opioid use disorder on buprenorphine (F11.20). No codeine cough syrup: codeine is an opioid he is in treatment for, and buprenorphine blocks much of its effect, so it could lead him to take more. Leftover codeine syrup should go to the take-back. Dextromethorphan cough medicines are also avoided, because with sertraline they add to the risk of serotonin toxicity. [S]
Continue buprenorphine with naloxone 8 mg twice daily.
Take the old cough syrup to the pharmacy take-back.

Obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42.2). The illness has stirred his contamination fears, and he has been seeking reassurance from his assistant many times a day. He was given the facts once, plainly; he and his therapist will treat further checking and questions as rituals to resist, as in exposure and response prevention. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone. [S]
Temperature checked once a day only.
Continue sertraline 100 mg and the exposure sessions, by telephone this week.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (2007); CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain - United States, 2022 (2022); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); Appropriate Antibiotic Use for Acute Respiratory Tract Infection in Adults: Advice for High-Value Care From the American College of Physicians and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (2016)

Follow-up: Ten-week review in three weeks. Return sooner for any of the warning signs above. Next scheduled visit 2026-07-13: ten-week review: sertraline to an OCD dose, exposure therapy and his staff's part in it, hearing aids and pain. [S]
